subject: Tenant segregation + egress controls — next technical steps
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@novuslabs.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: info@novuslabs.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 16:12:00 +0100
Subject: Follow-up from today — tenant segregation + outbound controls

Priya, thanks for the call earlier — that was helpful. Quick recap from our side and a few clarification requests so we can prioritize next steps with our compliance and infra teams.

Key drivers:
- Regulatory requirement: certain datasets (PHI-adjacent telemetry) must never leave EU jurisdiction or traverse public egress points without inspection.
- Procurement is asking for a network architecture that demonstrates egress controls and host isolation for inference endpoints.
- We are exploring an air-gapped or restricted-VPC option for higher-risk workloads; not all traffic needs that level, but some models will.

Open questions we need Redwood to confirm (technical):
1) Can Redwood Dedicated be deployed into our VPC with outbound-only bastion/egress via a customer-managed NAT or firewall?
2) Is there an option to force model-serving instances to use customer KMS (HSM) keys for any ephemeral artifact and logs?
3) How do you support prefix/KV cache isolation across tenants? We need to prove no cross-tenant leakage.

Attachments: I attached our high-level network segmentation (novus-network-segmentation-20261114.pdf).

Ideal next steps: a short 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra/ops and our NetOps + Infosec (we can do Tue 17 Nov or Thu 19 Nov 10:00–12:00 CET). Please confirm availability and any pre-reading.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Li
Head of Infrastructure, Novus Labs
---
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@novuslabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 18:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — tenant segregation + outbound controls

Sarah — great to meet you and the Novus team on the call. Appreciate the clear list of drivers; below is our agreed summary and proposed owners for each ask so nothing is lost.

Summary of pain/goals (as we heard):
- Goal: Run inference for sensitive workloads from EU-resident hosts with no unintended egress and demonstrable tenant isolation.
- Constraint: Procurement requires architecture that maps to their network controls and KMS policies.
- Preference: Private deployment (Dedicated in-customer VPC) if it allows customer-managed egress + KMS.

Redwood responses / next steps / owners:
1) VPC deployment + egress controls — owner: Ben Carter (Infra, cc'd). Ben: Redwood Dedicated supports customer-hosted NAT/firewall egress; we typically provision a set of private subnets and expose only the necessary outbound through customer-managed egress. We'll need your network diagram and allowed CIDR/port list to scope connectivity.

2) Customer KMS for ephemeral artifacts — owner: Priya (Product/Compliance). We support using customer-managed keys for at-rest model caches and logs when deployed in Private mode; detail to confirm with engineering on HSM-backed flows.

3) Cache & KV isolation — owner: Marissa Cole (Platform). Our runtime enforces tenant keying and namespace isolation; Marissa will prepare a one-pager and a small test plan demonstrating isolation and replay scenarios.

4) Evidence for procurement (SOC2 artifacts, encryption attestations, network diagrams) — owner: Priya. I'll attach an initial DOC with what we can supply and timelines.

Proposed cadence:
- Technical deep-dive: Tue 17 Nov 11:00 CET — Redwood infra (Ben + Marissa) + Priya (compliance) + Novus NetOps/Infosec. Can you confirm?
- Deliverables before the call: Novus network diagram (you already attached), allowed egress CIDRs/ports, and a short list of workloads that need air-gap behavior.

I attached a template (redwood-privacy-questions.xlsx) that procurement often finds helpful — fill the top sheet prior to Tue if possible.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Product Lead, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — tenant segregation + outbound controls

Looping in a couple quick notes from infra perspective:
- We can support egress via customer-managed NAT or dedicated egress appliances. We'll want to run through routing and webhook endpoints that Novus will need (metrics collection, health checks).
- HSM-backed KMS: feasible but will require a short engineering window to validate signing flows for ephemeral caches. Estimate: 5–7 business days to validate once we have access to a staging HSM endpoint.
- For the tech deep-dive on Tue 17 Nov 11:00 CET, I'll bring a checklist: network ports, IP allowlist, expected token lifetimes, and sample routing diagram.

Action items for Novus before Tue 17:
- Confirm Tue 17 11:00 CET or propose an alternate.
- Share list of hostnames IPs for any outbound dependencies (metrics, telemetry, updates).
- Mark which models/workloads are ‘high isolation’ vs. normal.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
